description: Use this skill when writing test-first, behavior-driven acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format for a Salesforce user story. Covers happy path, edge cases, negative paths, permission boundaries, and data-state preconditions so the AC block can drive UAT scripts and Apex test design downstream. Trigger keywords: given when then, gherkin, behavior driven AC, test first acceptance criteria, scenario outline, BDD acceptance criteria. NOT for the user-story format itself (use admin/user-story-writing-for-salesforce). NOT for UAT script writing (use admin/uat-test-case-design). NOT for Apex test method generation (use agents/test-class-generator). NOT for high-level UAT planning (use admin/uat-and-acceptance-criteria). More triggers: acceptance criteria record, ac_id, req_id on a criterion, artefact under test, negative case for a rule-type requirement, no-match fall-through criterion, oracle for a Then clause, test type apex flow manual, criteria linter, check_ac_format.py, --manifest-dir.
inputs: Draft user story (As a / I want / So that) with persona, object, and intended behavior
Target object and field-level requirements (FLS, required, picklist values)
Sharing context: OWD, role hierarchy position, permission set group assignments
Data-state preconditions: record ownership, related-record existence, lifecycle stage
Known constraints: governor limits, bulk volume, integration touchpoints
name: acceptance-criteria-given-when-then
official_sources: **Metadata API Developer Guide** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf — `AssignmentRules` / `AssignmentRule` (L23661–23713: rule entries are processed in container order — the ordering fact behind gotcha 10 and `worked-examples.md` AC-001.3); `AutoResponseRules` (L25196–25288: entry order selects the template, `senderEmail` / `template`, and the Classic-template packaging note behind REQ-002); `EscalationRules` (L59421–59499: container order, `businessHoursSource`, `escalationStartTime`, `disableEscalationWhenModified`, `minutesToEscalation` — REQ-003 and gotcha 12); `EntitlementProcess` (L59075–59217: versioned file naming, `minutesToComplete`, `useCriteriaStartTime`, and the negative-vs-positive `timeLength` that distinguishes a warning trigger from a violation trigger — REQ-004); `ValidationRule` (L45385–45403: `errorConditionFormula`, `errorDisplayField`, and the 255-character `errorMessage` limit — REQ-006); `PermissionSetObjectPermissions` (L95077–95113: `allowEdit` is an object-level capability while `modifyAllRecords` / `viewAllRecords` are the ones that apply "regardless of the sharing settings" — REQ-005); `CaseSettings` (L111700–111712, L112031–112033, L112133–112134: `defaultCaseOwner` as the assignment fall-through, `defaultCaseUser` as the Case History actor, and the two `caseOrigin` settings that make REQ-002's Web-vs-Email split testable); `Layout` / `FlexiPage` save options (L67423–67443, L82385–82403: whether the Case page even offers "Assign using active assignment rule" is a layout setting, which is why a manual-creation criterion has to name it).

**Object Reference for the Salesforce Platform** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/object_reference.pdf — `BusinessHours` (L53105–53108: "Escalation rules are run only during these hours", and holidays suspend both — the fact that separates a business-hours SLA from a clock SLA); `Case` (L62470–62477 `IsEscalated`, L62575–62587 `OwnerId` refers to Group **or** User, L62659–62666 `SlaStartDate`); `CaseHistory` (L62819, L63138–63139: history exists only for **tracked** fields — gotcha 13); `CaseMilestone` (L63342–63497: `TargetDate`, `IsCompleted`, `IsViolated`, `TimeRemainingInMins`, `BusinessHoursId` — the queryable oracle for REQ-004); `EmailMessage` (L103975–103976: available only to Email-to-Case / Enhanced Email orgs — the caveat on REQ-002's convenience query); `Group` (L154213–154226 `DoesIncludeBosses`, L154307–154342 `Type`, whose values include `Queue` — what makes `Owner.Type = 'Queue'` a real assertion).

**Apex Developer Guide** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_apex_developer_guide.pdf — Triggers and Order of Execution (L15442, L15449–15450, L15455–15457, L15461, L15471: validation at step 5 versus assignment 9, auto-response 10, escalation 12 and entitlement 15, plus the list of rules that do not re-run after a workflow field update — gotcha 9 and the split of REQ-006 into AC-006.1 / AC-006.3); `Database.DMLOptions.assignmentRuleHeader` (L8530–8569: `useDefaultRule` / `assignmentRuleId`, and the API 30.0+ change that leaves a record unassigned rather than falling to the default owner — gotcha 11); Mixed DML in test methods (L8905–8910: `System.runAs` is what makes REQ-005 automatable).

**Apex Reference Guide** — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexref.meta/apexref/ — `DmlOptions.AssignmentRuleHeader` (L148033–148034: `useDefaultRule` "affects only the default assignment rule and does not disable other existing assignment rules on the object" — the reason an Apex criterion must name which rule it is exercising).

**Data Loader Guide** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_data_loader.pdf — the **Assignment rule** setting (L379–383: blank by default, and when set it "overrides Owner values in your CSV file") — one of the three disagreeing entry paths in gotcha 11 and the reason `worked-examples.md` AC-001.4 is manual.

**Bulk API 2.0 Developer Guide** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_asynch.pdf — job resource `assignmentRuleId` (L1591–1595: **Optional**, so absent means no rule runs) — the second disagreeing entry path.

**REST API Developer Guide** — https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf — Assignment Rule Header (L691–694: "If the header is not provided with a request, REST API defaults to using the active assignment rules") — the third, and the one that inverts the default.

**Repo standards and sibling artefacts** — `standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md` (cited rather than restated: the AC never names the automation tool, per gotcha 3); `admin/requirements-traceability-matrix` § ID Conventions (the `REQ-nnn` convention every criterion joins on); `admin/requirements-gathering-for-sf` § The Requirements Catalogue (the `downstream.fit_gap_row` pairing that makes `FG-XXX` and `REQ-XXX` one-to-one); `admin/configuration-workbook-authoring` § Per-Row Schema (`source_req_id`, the column the criteria feed); `admin/uat-and-acceptance-criteria/references/worked-examples.md` §§ 2.3, 3 (the persona roster and the `ac_id` column these criteria supply); `skills/admin/case-management-setup/references/worked-example-case-intake.md` (the build under test).
outputs: Given/When/Then acceptance criteria block ready to paste into the user story
Scenario outline (Examples table) for parameterized cases
Negative-path AC list paired one-to-one with each happy-path AC
Permission and data-state precondition block with explicit user/PSG references
Handoff notes pointing test-class-generator agent at the bulk and edge scenarios
Lintable acceptance-criteria record (YAML or markdown table) carrying req_id, persona, sandbox, seed data, artefact, proof and test type per criterion
